title: Intrinsic rewards guide visual resource allocation via reinforcement learning
title_zh: 内在奖励通过强化学习引导视觉资源分配
abstract: Abstract Humans and other animals prioritize visual processing of stimuli that signal rewards. While previous research has focused on tangible incentives (for example, money or food), the effects of intrinsic incentives—such as perceived competence—are less well understood. Here, across a series of visual estimation experiments, we manipulated observers’ subjective sense of confidence in their judgements using either deceptive trial-by-trial feedback or real discrepancies in stimulus reliability. We found that observers prioritized encoding of stimuli associated with lower uncertainty or error, benefiting performance for stimuli already estimated accurately, while further impairing performance for those estimated poorly. These reward-driven biases, while potentially adaptive, impaired overall accuracy in the present tasks by causing resource allocation to deviate from the error-minimizing strategy. To account for these findings, we supplemented a normalization model of neural resource allocation with a simple reinforcement learning rule. Intrinsic and external rewards cumulatively shaped the values assigned to different stimuli by the model, and the resulting discrepancies biased resource allocation and thereby estimation error, quantitatively matching the data. These findings reveal how intrinsic reward signals can shape resource allocation in ways that are both adaptive and counterproductive, offering a computational basis for the motivational biases underlying cognitive performance.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人类及其他动物倾向于优先处理能提示奖励的视觉刺激。此前的研究多聚焦于可触及的激励（如金钱或食物），而内在激励（如对自身能力的感知）对视觉处理的影响尚不充分了解。本研究通过一系列视觉估计实验，利用欺骗性逐试反馈或真实的刺激可靠性差异，操纵观察者对其判断的自信感。结果显示，观察者更倾向于编码与较低不确定性或误差相关的刺激，从而提升已准确估计刺激的表现，但进一步削弱对估计不佳刺激的表现。这种奖励驱动的偏差虽然可能具有适应性，却通过使资源分配偏离最小化误差的策略，整体降低了任务准确性。为解释这些发现，我们在神经资源分配的归一化模型中加入了简单的强化学习规则。内在与外部奖励共同塑造模型对不同刺激的价值评估，导致的价值差异偏向资源分配，从而影响估计误差，定量匹配了实验数据。这些结果揭示了内在奖励信号如何以既适应又有害的方式塑造资源分配，为认知表现中动机偏差提供了计算基础。
